content:
I think the answer to the question in the title should be affirmative, but I'm looking at this in Mathlib:

noncomputable instance UniformSpace.Completion.instNormedFieldOfCompletableTopField(A : Type u_3) [NormedField A] [CompletableTopField A] :
NormedField (Completion A)

Doc URL: https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Module/Completion.html#UniformSpace.Completion.instNormedFieldOfCompletableTopField

Why should we explicitly assume that A is completable? There is already an instance

instance NormedField.instCompletableTopField{F : Type u_1} [NormedField F] :
CompletableTopField F

Doc URL: https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Field/Instances.html#NormedField.instCompletableTopField

So theoretically, the instance CompletableTopField A should be automatically inferred?

Hmm, it IS automatically inferred after I import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Field.Instances, the file where NormedField.instCompletableTopField lives.

So the question becomes: is there a particular reason that Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Field.Instances is not imported by Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.Completion?

Basically for performance reasons. To complete modules you don't need all the material that is imported by Normed.Field.Instances, but you can try to open a PR, add the import and then see how much this affects compilation. But why do you want to do so?

Reason: I'm just curious why UniformSpace.Completion.instNormedFieldOfCompletableTopField needs CompletableTopField F in its statement, as this condition seems to be implicated by the NormedField instance. Anyway, this is not a big problem.
A PR explaining this in its docstring would probably be reasonable
